The bracket is modelled and all four exports succeeded. No step failed, apart from one early retry described below.

**Model:** the base plate is a box `width` × 60 × 4. The back plate is a box `width` × 4 × 50, joined to the base at the corner. The two Ø5 holes are cylinders cut along Y through the back plate at Z = 35. They sit at X = `width/2 − 20` and `width/2 + 20`, so they stay 40 mm apart and centred when the width changes.

The first batch failed because `width` wasn't defined yet. It rolled back with no changes, I created the parameter, and the rerun succeeded.

**Exports and bounding boxes (mm):**

| Width | Files | Bounding box min → max | Hole centres (X, Z) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 80 | `/lab/out/bracket-80.step`, `/lab/out/bracket-80.stl` | (0, 0, 0) → (80, 60, 50) | (20, 35) and (60, 35) |
| 100 | `/lab/out/bracket-100.step`, `/lab/out/bracket-100.stl` | (0, 0, 0) → (100, 60, 50) | (30, 35) and (70, 35) |

I read the 80 mm box from `measure` and the hole centres from `body_topology`. For 100 mm I only checked `body_topology` (edges and cylinder origins), not `measure`, so its bounding box comes from the edge coordinates: X up to 100, Y up to 60, Z up to 50. Changing the parameter recomputed all 4 features without errors.

The two STL files are both 20,284 bytes. I expected that, because both have the same face and triangle counts. I didn't open the exported files.
